pages.title: Pasta night with my roommate · 1/3
paragraphs: On Sunday night, my roommate Aaron and I cooked together in our small kitchen. He opened the fridge and asked, “**What are you making?**” I smiled and said, “**Pasta with tomato sauce**.”

Aaron wanted to help. “**Can I help?**” he asked. “**Sure**,” I said. “**Cut the onions, please**.” He took a knife and a cutting board. “**How many?**” he asked. “**Just one**,” I said. “Then **add the tomatoes**.”
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: Pasta night with my roommate · 2/3
paragraphs: I put a big pan on the stove and added some oil and a little salt. The kitchen smelled so good! Aaron came near the stove, and I said, “**Careful! The pan is hot**.” He stepped back and laughed.

My family always says that cooking is like a game. First you cut, then you fry, next you add, and finally you taste. I thought about the fairy tale The Magic Porridge Pot, with a small pot that cooks porridge by magic. We have no magic pot, but tonight we made pasta, and it was a lot of fun.

pages.title: Pasta night with my roommate · 3/3
paragraphs: When the sauce was ready, I put the pasta on two plates. Aaron looked at his plate and said, “**Dinner is served!**” We sat at the small table and ate slowly. The food was simple, but it was delicious.

items.why: Smelled = had an odor.

items.q: He stepped back and laughed. O que significa “stepped back”?
items.why: Stepped back = moved away from something.

items.q: The food was simple, but it was delicious. O que significa “delicious”?
items.why: Delicious = tastes great.
